# Spaces

<!-- generated by scripts/spaces.mjs --md from test/space/registry.js, scripts/decision-points.mjs, test/space/git-manifest.json and test/space/ratchet.json; test/space/registry.test.js fails if it drifts -->

Every decision ply makes, and every check git makes on the same input, belongs to a **space**: a list of axes, each a tagged union, whose product is explored cell by cell and judged by real git. Random fuzzing finds a bug; only enumeration says a bug class is gone (#52 could not tell broken from fixed by fuzzing; the enumerated #51 and #62 spaces found 412,008 and 3,598 wrong cells).

The procedure is enforced, not remembered:

- `scripts/decision-points.mjs` extracts every decision point from `src/` (each `fail(`/`failHere(` call, each call to a fail wrapper, each produced error code, each untyped `throw new Error`, each exported `parse*`/`decode*`/`classify*`/`decide*`).
- `scripts/git-manifest.mjs` extracts git v2.50.0's own checks (fsck msg ids, die/error/ng/reject strings of the protocol files, capabilities, request arguments, ref-name rules, fsck_tree modes) into `test/space/git-manifest.json`.
- `test/space/registry.js` maps each one to the space and axis that covers it, or excludes it with a reason.
- Gates (`test/space/registry.test.js`, `test/space/failsites.test.js`, in CI): **a** every decision point is registered; **b** every git check is covered or excluded; **c** every fail site is reached by a cell (stacks recorded at `plyError` by `test/space/failsite-hook.mjs` in node and by the plugin in `vitest.config.ts` under vitest: `src/` and the bundle are untouched), and every site the registry gives a merged space is reached by that space. A category with holes is in REPORT mode (holes printed; only a hole not in `test/space/ratchet.json` fails); at 0 it switches to ENFORCE. The ratchet only goes down: `npm run spaces -- --ratchet`.

| git | 2 | REPORT |
| failsites | 30 | REPORT |
| claims | 0 | ENFORCE |
| linux | 0 | ENFORCE |
| stale | 0 | ENFORCE |

Decision points: **717** (633 fail sites, 20 produced codes, 2 untyped throws, 37 exported parse/decode/classify/decide functions). Covered by a merged space 617, by a pending PR 45, excluded 29, unregistered 26. Fail sites no cell reaches: 30 of 633. Of the registered points, 220 are claimed by an enumerated space, 9 only by a random one and 433 only by a curated list: a curated or random claim says a case exists, not that the class is gone.

git v2.50.0 checks: **377** (fsck-msg 71, error 38, die 111, reject 44, ng 2, err-pkt 2, capability 46, request-arg 21, refname-rule 18, tree-mode 24). Covered by a merged space 233, by a pending PR 0, excluded 142, uncovered 2. Claimed by an enumerated space 221, random 2, curated 10.

¹ OS-dependent cells: expectations come from what the git server does on that run, fixtures keep refs in reftable (git ≥ 2.46, fix/43-bom 716cd77), and the Linux run in CI is the pass of record (the `linux` gate: every merged CI space's runners must have a Linux record; a macOS pass never counts).

- `tree-name-alphabet`: core.protectHFS / protectNTFS default per platform (HFS on macOS, NTFS on Windows): the same name can be refused by a checkout on one OS and not another
- `git-bytes`: APFS cannot store a non-UTF-8 ref name as a loose ref file (EILSEQ): on macOS with the files backend those cells degrade to both-refuse; reftable fixtures since 716cd77
- `push-tree`: filesFromDir reads the local filesystem (exec bits, symlinks, case): what exists to push differs by OS
- `checkout-tree`: writes the tree to the local filesystem: case-insensitive (APFS default) and Unicode-normalizing filesystems collide names Linux keeps apart
- `edit-fuzz`: the harness writes generated paths to disk: on a case-insensitive filesystem `a` and `A` collide (EEXIST, observed on macOS 2026-10-31)

## Decode sites (25: lossless 10, strict 3, replacement 12)

git passes ref names, tree entry names, messages, idents and paths through as raw bytes. A **strict** decode (fatal TextDecoder, decodeURIComponent) refuses what git accepts; a **replacement** decode (the default TextDecoder) turns non-UTF-8 into U+FFFD and loses it. Either is a severity-1 hole unless the registry excludes it as display text or protocol keywords; the fix is a lossless decode and a space with a non-UTF-8 content axis.

| where | mode | via | registry |

| `src/bytes.ts` encodeBytes() | lossless | decodeBytes | `git-bytes` / content |

## Holes (54)

Ranked by severity, then category (`git`: a git check with no space; `decisions`: a ply decision point with no registry entry; `failsites`: a fail site no cell reaches; `claims`: a registry claim its space does not back). Fail-site and claim holes are the ratchet's, from the last recorded run.
